touches.text: Transport: as fast as we can make it, settled by measuring on this box, not by choosing. Inside a Linux box the bus is our own small broker on Unix sockets, routing by name (measured 50 µs a round trip, against 110 for Postgres NOTIFY and 250 for NATS). Between boxes, and on Windows (Python there has no AF_UNIX), it is TCP, speaking TLS with pinned certificate fingerprints checked both ways; cairn install makes each box's certificate. WHY TLS: no tunnel, nothing extra to set up.
A Unix socket path cannot be longer than 108 bytes, so a socket address is kept short and never nests deep in a device tree.

Scratch bus: a proof needs a bus it controls (a real store, stub devices, nobody live listening), so the cairn device publishes scratch_bus, the way db_domain's client carries scratch(). 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):
Test tiers: commit, hourly, daily and weekly. Each tier runs only what it must, so a commit needs only its own proofs and the long runs wait for the long tiers; nothing runs just in case.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
